chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn 'Udhafir from Umar ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
If you are walking, then proclaim your Ihlal and Talbiyah loudly from the Masjid, and if you are riding, then when your white mount raises you up

key_terms.إِهْلَال: The declaration of entering the state of Ihram for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.المَسْجِد: The Masjid, specifically referring to the Masjid al-Haram in this context
key_terms.تَلْبِيَة: The specific supplication 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk' recited during Hajj
key_terms.رَاحِلَة: A mount or beast of burden

ai.seo_question: How should one recite the Talbiyah when walking versus riding during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar delineates the specific protocols for vocalizing the Talbiyah during Hajj, distinguishing between the modes of travel to ensure the declaration is audible yet appropriate to the pilgrim's state. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the public manifestation of the Hajj rites, linking the physical act of travel with the spiritual proclamation of 'Labbayk'. The instruction to wait until the mount rises before speaking loudly while riding highlights a nuanced understanding of comfort and decorum in ritual practice.
